design.text: Randomized (1:1), open-label, single center trial in Vietnam comparing Egaten 10 mg/kg x 2 (12 hours apart) vs. artesunate 4 mg/kg once a day for 10 days in acute fascioliasis.

Patients were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive either two doses of Egaten® 10 mg/kg 12 hours apart or artesunate (b) (4) 4 mg/kg once a day for 10 days. All patients were hospitalized for 10 days and had directly-observed therapy for study drug. Food intake at the time of study treatment was unspecified.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: resolution of abdominal pain at hospital discharge (day 10).

citations.quote: **Primary Endpoint:** Resolution of abdominal pain at hospital discharge (day 10)
The Hien study was a randomized controlled trial comparing TCBZ at 10 mg/kg q12h x 2 (N=50) vs. artesunate (N=50) for the treatment of patients with acute fascioliasis.

result.text: On the primary endpoint (no abdominal pain at discharge), TCBZ was numerically inferior to the comparator artesunate: 44/50 (88%) vs. 50/50 (100%), diff -12% (95% CI -21.5, -1.5; p=0.027), i.e., TCBZ did not beat artesunate on the primary endpoint. At 3 months post-treatment (a secondary outcome), 92% (46/50) and 76% (38/50) of patients in the TCBZ and artesunate arms respectively had no clinical symptoms (risk difference 16%; 95% CI 1.7%, 30.8%; p=0.035), favoring TCBZ.

target_moa.text: Triclabendazole is an anthelmintic (benzimidazole derivative); its mechanism against Fasciola is not fully understood but the drug and its active metabolites penetrate the fluke tegument, altering the resting tegumental membrane potential, interfering with microtubule structure and function, and inhibiting protein and enzyme synthesis, resulting in death of the fluke.

citations.quote: The mechanism of action of TCBZ is incompletely understood but studies suggest that the drug and its metabolites penetrate through the tegument of immature and adult *Fasciola* flukes leading to an alteration of the resting tegumental membrane potential, interference with microtubule structure and function, and inhibition of protein and enzyme synthesis resulting in death of the fluke.
TCBZ and its active metabolites have been shown to cause structural damage and impair the motility of Fasciola hepatica and Fasciola gigantica.

EGATEN (triclabendazole) tablet is an orally administered anthelmintic for immediate release. Triclabendazole is designated chemically as benzimidazole derivative, 6-chloro-5-(2, 3-dichlorophenoxy)-2-(methylthio)-1H-benzimidazole (triclabendazole).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>2%) at the 20 mg/kg dose are abdominal pain, hyperhidrosis, nausea, decreased appetite, headache, urticaria, diarrhea, vomiting, musculoskeletal chest pain, and pruritus. Abdominal pain was very common (56% at 10 mg/kg; 93% at 20 mg/kg). Triclabendazole may prolong the QT interval.
